quote: Donovan and Freislich call a matrix problem "wild" if it contains the matrix pair problem and "tame" otherwise, in analogy with the partition of animals into wild and tame ones.
note: The terminology "wild" and "tame" for classification problems was introduced in Donovan and Freislich 1972, with more precise definitions published in 1973. The wild problem specifically refers to the problem of classifying pairs of n×n matrices under simultaneous conjugation.
